title: Are You Okay?
subtitle: Four ways to show concern
review: Text and notes written by Claude: check them. No Burmese yet.
intro: A sleepless night with a known cause, a bike accident and a very small dog, a dinner guest who does not arrive and a laptop that is 'resting': four short scenes between Emma and Lucas. Listen for how they ask what is wrong, and for the answers that say very little.

lines.text: Hey. You look tired. Are you okay?
lines.note: You look + adjective: You look tired. Are you okay? is the first question to ask.
I'm fine: the usual answer, even when it is not true.

lines.text: Are you sure? You don't look fine.
lines.note: Are you sure? Ask again when the person does not look fine.
Not… at all = zero.

lines.text: Oh no. What's wrong? Do you want to talk about it?
lines.note: What's wrong? asks about the problem. Do you want to talk about it? offers to listen.
Snore: make a loud noise when you sleep.
That's terrible: for bad news.
Take a guess = try to answer. She means: it was you.

lines.text: Lucas! What happened? Are you all right?
lines.note: What happened? asks about something that is finished. Are you all right? = Are you okay?
Fell off: past of fall off.
Does it hurt? asks about pain in the body.

lines.text: My knee hurts. And my pride.
lines.note: My knee hurts. Pride: your good feeling about yourself.

lines.text: Poor thing. How did it happen?
lines.note: Poor thing! shows you feel sorry for the person. Friendly and informal.

lines.text: A dog ran in front of me. A huge dog.
lines.note: Ran: past of run. Huge = very, very big.
This little guy? She means the small dog.

lines.text: He looked bigger at the time.
lines.note: At the time = when it happened.

lines.text: Here's some ice. Is the dog okay?
lines.note: Ice: frozen water, good for a knee that hurts.

lines.text: … The dog is fine. Thanks for asking.
lines.note: Thanks for asking: polite. Here Lucas is not happy: she asked about the dog, not about him.
I'm worried: I think something bad happened.

lines.text: Me too. He's never late for dinner.
lines.note: Me too = I am worried too.
Do you think something happened? = something bad.

lines.text: I hope not. Should we call him?
lines.note: I hope not = I hope nothing bad happened. Should we…? asks for advice.

lines.text: He's not answering. What if he's sick?
lines.note: What if…? imagines a bad possibility.
Lost: he cannot find the way.

lines.text: Wait. What day did you tell him?
… So he's fine. That's a relief.
lines.note: That's a relief: said when the worry is over.

lines.text: Emma… do you have a minute?
lines.note: Do you have a minute? = Can I talk to you?
You look worried. What's wrong?
It's nothing = it is not serious. Don't worry = stop worrying.

lines.text: Now I'm worried. What's the matter?
lines.note: What's the matter? = What's wrong?

lines.text: Lucas. What happened to my laptop?
lines.note: What happened to…? asks about a thing or a person.
Resting: not working for a short time. The laptop is broken.
Why? = why do you ask?
While it lasts = for the short time it continues. Emma means: you will not be fine soon.

notes: First questions: Are you okay? Are you all right? What's wrong? What's the matter?
What happened? asks about something that is finished: a fall, an accident, bad news.
You look + adjective says what you notice: You look tired. You look worried.
Are you sure? asks again when someone says I'm fine but does not look fine.
I'm worried. What if…? Do you think something happened? are for a person who is not there.
Short answers: I'm fine. It's nothing. Don't worry. When the worry is over: That's a relief.

questions.q: Your friend is sitting on the ground next to his bike. What do you ask?
questions.why: What happened? asks about something that is finished, like a fall.

questions.q: “Are you okay?” “I'm fine.” Your friend does not look fine. What do you say?
questions.why: Are you sure? asks again, gently.

questions.q: Paul is late and he is not answering his phone. What does Emma say?
questions.why: I'm worried = I think something bad happened.

questions.q: Paul is fine: dinner is tomorrow. What does Lucas say?
questions.why: That's a relief: the worry is over.
